answer: A newcomer must cross a canyon of cost before it can transact: lock a refundable deposit and complete small verifiable tasks checked by randomly assigned peers, earning a signed receipt for each one. Each receipt acts like a lantern carried through the dark, proving real work was done and lighting the path toward trust, while the growing relic of past verified output — a hash-chained ledger of receipts — makes history impossible to fake cheaply. A Sybil attacker must pay the deposit and do the work for every single fake identity, so bulk forgery costs more than it can ever earn.
